strength.name: Strength
strength.description: Build maximal force with heavier loads and lower reps, usually 1 to 6 reps per set.

hypertrophy.name: Hypertrophy
hypertrophy.description: Build muscle size with moderate weight and moderate reps, usually 6 to 15 reps per set.

endurance.name: Muscular Endurance
endurance.description: Improve how long muscles can work with lighter weight and higher reps, usually 15 or more reps per set.

power.name: Power
power.description: Develop explosive speed and force, often with fast bar speed or plyometric movements.

mobility.name: Mobility
mobility.description: Improve joint range of motion and controlled movement quality through dynamic drills and positions.

stability.name: Stability
stability.description: Train balance, bracing, and control, often with core-focused or single-leg work.

cardio.name: Cardio
cardio.description: Raise heart rate and improve conditioning with sustained or interval-based aerobic work.

pilates.name: Pilates
pilates.description: Controlled, low-impact training focused on core strength, alignment, and breath, often on a mat or reformer.

stretching.name: Stretching
stretching.description: Improve flexibility and recovery with held stretches and lengthening-focused movements.

general.name: General Fitness
general.description: Mixed training for overall health and movement, not tied to one specific performance goal.

push.name: Push
push.description: Move weight away from your body. Includes horizontal presses like bench press and vertical presses like overhead press.

pull.name: Pull
pull.description: Move weight toward your body. Includes rows, pull-ups, and pulldowns that train the back and biceps.

hinge.name: Hinge
hinge.description: Bend at the hips with a flat back. Includes deadlifts, Romanian deadlifts, and hip thrusts that target the posterior chain.

squat.name: Squat
squat.description: Bend at the knees and hips together with an upright torso. Includes back squats, front squats, and goblet squats.

lunge.name: Lunge
lunge.description: Step into a split stance and lower your body. Includes walking lunges, reverse lunges, and split squats.

carry.name: Carry
carry.description: Walk while holding weight. Includes farmer carries, suitcase carries, and overhead carries for grip, core, and conditioning.

rotation.name: Rotation
rotation.description: Rotate through the torso or hips under load or control. Includes cable chops, wood chops, and rotational throws.

core.name: Core
core.description: Train the midsection through bracing, flexion, or anti-movement. Includes planks, crunches, leg raises, and pallof presses.

isolation.name: Isolation
isolation.description: Focus on one joint and one muscle group with minimal help from other muscles. Includes curls, extensions, flies, and lateral raises.

stretch.name: Stretch
stretch.description: Lengthen muscles and open joints through controlled, held, or repeated end-range movement. Includes chest openers, static stretches, and flexibility-focused drills.

beginner.name: Beginner
beginner.description: Suitable for people new to training or an exercise. Simple setup, easy to learn form, and lower coordination demands.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.description: For trainees with solid basic form who can handle more setup, balance, or technique. Requires some training experience.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: For experienced lifters. Higher skill, stability, or loading demands and less room for form breakdown.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with a barbell while lying on a flat bench.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes under the bar, feet planted, and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar, lower it under control to your lower chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back
Keep your feet planted
Control the bar on the way down
Do not bounce the bar off your chest

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with a barbell on an incline bench to emphasize the upper chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline, lie back with your eyes under the bar, feet planted on the floor, and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar, lower it under control to your upper chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down
Keep your feet planted and glutes on the bench
Control the bar on the way down to your upper chest
Do not bounce the bar off your chest
Avoid setting the incline too steep, which shifts work away from the chest

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with a barbell on a decline bench to emphasize the lower chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a slight decline, secure your legs in the foot pads, lie back with your eyes under the bar, and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar, lower it under control to your lower chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down
Keep your legs secured and your body stable on the bench
Control the bar on the way down to your lower chest
Do not bounce the bar off your chest
Avoid flaring your elbows too wide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with dumbbells while lying on a flat bench, allowing each arm to move independently.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, feet planted, and the dumbbells held at chest level with your palms facing forward.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are extended, lower them under control to chest level, and repeat.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back
Keep your feet planted and glutes on the bench
Control the dumbbells on the way down
Do not let the dumbbells drift too far apart at the top
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with dumbbells on an incline bench to emphasize the upper chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline, sit with a dumbbell in each hand, lie back, and hold the dumbbells at chest level with your palms facing forward.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are extended, lower them under control to upper chest level, and repeat.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down
Keep your feet planted and glutes on the bench
Control the dumbbells on the way down to your upper chest
Do not let the dumbbells drift too far apart at the top
Avoid setting the incline too steep, which shifts work away from the chest

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound chest press performed with dumbbells on a decline bench to emphasize the lower chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a slight decline, secure your legs in the foot pads, lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, and hold them at chest level with your palms facing forward.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are extended, lower them under control to lower chest level, and repeat.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down
Keep your legs secured and your body stable on the bench
Control the dumbbells on the way down to your lower chest
Do not let the dumbbells drift too far apart at the top
Avoid flaring your elbows too wide

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation chest exercise performed with dumbbells on a flat bench, using a wide arcing motion to stretch and contract the chest.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows and palms facing each other.
exercises.instructions: Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest, then squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together above your chest.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
Lower the dumbbells with control; do not drop them below shoulder level
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your back flat on the bench
Squeeze your chest at the top without letting the dumbbells touch
Use a lighter weight than you would for pressing movements

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation chest exercise performed with dumbbells on an incline bench, using a wide arcing motion to emphasize the upper chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline, lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your upper chest with a slight bend in your elbows and palms facing each other.
exercises.instructions: Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your upper chest, then squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together above your upper chest.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
Lower the dumbbells with control; do not drop them below shoulder level
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your glutes on the bench
Squeeze your chest at the top without letting the dumbbells touch
Avoid setting the incline too steep, which shifts work away from the chest

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation chest exercise performed with dumbbells on a decline bench, using a wide arcing motion to emphasize the lower chest.
exercises.setup: Set the bench to a slight decline, secure your legs in the foot pads, lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your lower chest with a slight bend in your elbows and palms facing each other.
exercises.instructions: Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your lower chest, then squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together above your lower chest.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
Lower the dumbbells with control; do not drop them below shoulder level
Keep your legs secured and your body stable on the bench
Squeeze your chest at the top without letting the dumbbells touch
Use a lighter weight than you would for pressing movements

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight chest exercise performed from a high plank position, lowering your chest toward the floor and pressing back up.
exercises.setup: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers forward, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
exercises.instructions: Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then press through your hands to return to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your core braced and your hips in line with your shoulders
Lower with control; do not let your lower back sag
Keep your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso
Press all the way up without shrugging your shoulders
Modify on your knees if full push-ups are too difficult

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation chest exercise using cables set at chest height, bringing the handles together in a wide arcing motion.
exercises.setup: Set both cable pulleys to chest height, grab a handle in each hand, and step forward into a slight stagger stance with a soft bend in your elbows.
exercises.instructions: Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a controlled arc, squeeze at the center, then return with control to the stretched position.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout
Squeeze your chest at the center; do not let your shoulders roll forward
Control the weight on the way back; do not let the stack slam
Keep your torso upright and your core braced
Adjust pulley height to target flat, incline, or decline emphasis

exercises.name: Cable Crossover
exercises.description: A standing cable chest exercise where high pulleys are brought down and together in front of the hips or lower chest.
exercises.setup: Set both cable pulleys above shoulder height, grab the handles, and step forward with a slight forward lean and soft elbows.
exercises.instructions: Pull the handles down and together across your body in a sweeping motion, squeeze your chest, then return with control to the start.
formCues: Use a slight forward lean and a stable stagger stance
Keep a soft bend in your elbows; do not turn this into a press
Squeeze your chest hard at the bottom of the arc
Control the eccentric; do not let the cables yank your arms back
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.description: A compound bodyweight press performed on parallel bars with a forward lean to emphasize the chest.
exercises.setup: Grip parallel bars, support yourself at arm's length, and lean your torso slightly forward with your legs behind you or bent.
exercises.instructions: Lower your body by bending your elbows until you feel a stretch in your chest, then press back up to full arm extension.
formCues: Lean forward to shift emphasis to the chest rather than the triceps
Lower with control; do not drop into the bottom position
Keep your shoulders down and avoid excessive shoulder shrug at the top
Do not flare your elbows straight out to the sides
Use an assisted dip machine or band if bodyweight is too difficult

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
exercises.description: A machine-based chest fly that guides your arms through a fixed arc for consistent chest isolation.
exercises.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest height, sit with your back flat against the pad, and grip the handles or place your forearms on the pads.
exercises.instructions: Bring the handles or pads together in front of your chest, squeeze, then return with control until you feel a stretch in your chest.
formCues: Keep your back flat against the pad throughout
Do not let your shoulders roll forward at the finish
Use a controlled tempo; do not slam the weight stack
Stop when you feel a stretch; do not overextend your shoulders
Keep your feet planted and your core lightly braced

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.description: A pressing exercise using a barbell anchored in a landmine setup, pressing the bar up and forward at an angle.
exercises.setup: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine base or corner, load the free end, and stand or kneel facing the bar with both hands on the end of the bar.
exercises.instructions: Press the bar up and forward until your arms are extended, then lower with control back toward your chest or upper chest.
formCues: Brace your core to stay stable during the press
Press in a smooth arc; do not twist your torso excessively
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows at the bottom
Control the bar on the way down
Use one arm at a time for a greater stability challenge

exercises.name: Floor Press
exercises.description: A barbell bench press variation performed lying on the floor, limiting range of motion at the bottom to reduce shoulder stress.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, position yourself under a barbell in a rack or have a partner hand you the bar, and grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Lower the bar until your upper arms rest on the floor, pause briefly, then press the bar up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Stop when your upper arms touch the floor; do not bounce
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back during the press
Drive through your feet and keep your glutes on the floor
Control the bar; the pause at the bottom removes momentum
Use a spotter or safety pins when lifting heavy

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.description: A chest and lat exercise performed lying on a bench, lowering a dumbbell in an arc behind your head and pulling it back over your chest.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted, hold one dumbbell with both hands on the inside of the weight plate, and extend it above your chest.
exercises.instructions: Lower the dumbbell in a slow arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats, then pull it back over your chest to the starting position.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout
Move only at the shoulders; do not arch your lower back excessively
Lower with control; do not drop the weight behind you
Keep your hips low on the bench for stability
Use a manageable weight; this is not a maximal press

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: A chest press performed on a Smith machine with a fixed bar path for added stability compared to a free barbell.
exercises.setup: Set a flat bench under the Smith machine bar, lie back with your eyes under the bar, and grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists, lower it under control to your chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Position the bench so the bar path lines up with your lower chest
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your feet planted
Do not bounce the bar off your chest
Lock the bar out fully before re-racking
Use a spotter mindset even on a Smith; re-rack with control

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight push-up with your hands elevated on a bench or box to reduce load and emphasize the upper chest.
exercises.setup: Place your hands on a sturdy bench or box slightly wider than shoulder-width and walk your feet back into a high plank with your body in a straight line.
exercises.instructions: Lower your chest toward the bench by bending your elbows, then press back up to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your core braced and your body in a straight line
Lower with control; do not let your hips sag
Keep your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso
Use a higher surface to make the exercise easier if needed
Progress to lower surfaces as you get stronger

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight push-up with your feet elevated on a bench to increase difficulty and emphasize the lower chest.
exercises.setup: Place your feet on a sturdy bench and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width in a high plank position.
exercises.instructions: Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension.
formCues: Keep your core tight so your hips do not drop
Lower under control; do not face-plant from the elevated position
Keep your elbows from flaring straight out to the sides
Press through your palms and squeeze your chest at the top
Start with a low elevation if full decline push-ups are too hard

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up variation with hands placed wider than standard to increase chest involvement and reduce triceps emphasis.
exercises.setup: Start in a high plank with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
exercises.instructions: Lower your chest toward the floor, then press back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Do not place your hands so wide that your shoulders feel strained
Keep your core braced throughout the movement
Lower with control and maintain a straight body line
Press through your chest rather than just your arms
Modify on your knees if needed

exercises.name: Incline Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: An incline chest press on a Smith machine with a fixed bar path to target the upper chest with added stability.
exercises.setup: Set an incline bench to 30 to 45 degrees under the Smith machine bar, lie back, and grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar, lower it under control to your upper chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Align the bench so the bar tracks to your upper chest
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your feet planted
Do not bounce the bar off your chest
Avoid setting the incline too steep
Re-rack the bar with control at the end of each set

exercises.name: Decline Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: A decline chest press on a Smith machine with a fixed bar path to emphasize the lower chest.
exercises.setup: Set a decline bench under the Smith machine bar, secure your legs, lie back, and grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
exercises.instructions: Unrack the bar, lower it under control to your lower chest, then press it back up until your arms are extended.
formCues: Keep your legs secured and your body stable on the bench
Control the bar on the way down to your lower chest
Do not bounce the bar off your chest
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down
Lock out fully before re-racking

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: A seated chest press on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine with a fixed pressing path.
exercises.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest height, sit with your back flat against the pad, and grip the handles.
exercises.instructions: Press the handles forward until your arms are extended, then return with control until you feel a stretch in your chest.
formCues: Keep your back flat against the pad throughout
Do not lock out aggressively or shrug your shoulders
Control the weight on the way back; do not let the stack slam
Keep your feet planted for stability
Use a full range of motion without overextending your shoulders

exercises.name: Incline Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: An incline chest press on a machine with a fixed path to target the upper chest with minimal setup.
exercises.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles align with upper-chest height, sit with your back against the incline pad, and grip the handles.
exercises.instructions: Press the handles up and forward until your arms are extended, then return with control to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your back and head in contact with the pad
Press through your upper chest; do not shrug at the top
Use a controlled tempo on the way down
Keep your feet planted and your core lightly braced
Stop just short of pain in the shoulder joint

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A unilateral dumbbell bench press that challenges chest strength and core stability one arm at a time.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on a bench with one dumbbell held at chest level, feet planted, and your free arm extended to the side or resting on your hip for balance.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbell up until your arm is extended, lower it under control to chest level, and complete all reps before switching arms.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back on the bench
Brace your core to prevent your torso from rotating
Control the dumbbell; do not let it drift out to the side
Keep your wrist stacked over your elbow
Use slightly lighter weight than your two-arm bench press

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.description: A dumbbell press performed lying on the floor, stopping when your upper arms touch the ground to limit shoulder stress.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level with your upper arms on the floor.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are extended, lower until your upper arms rest on the floor, pause briefly, and repeat.
formCues: Stop when your upper arms touch the floor; do not bounce
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back during the press
Control the dumbbells; do not let them drift apart at the top
Drive through your feet for stability
Use a neutral or palms-forward grip based on comfort

exercises.name: Resistance Band Chest Press
exercises.description: A standing or floor chest press using resistance bands anchored behind you for home-friendly pressing.
exercises.setup: Anchor a resistance band at chest height behind you, hold a handle in each hand, and step forward until there is tension with your hands at chest level.
exercises.instructions: Press the handles forward until your arms are extended, squeeze your chest, then return with control to the starting position.
formCues: Stand in a stable stagger stance with your core braced
Press straight forward; do not let your shoulders roll forward
Control the band on the way back; do not let it snap you backward
Adjust your distance from the anchor to change difficulty
Keep your wrists neutral throughout

exercises.name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
exercises.description: A home-friendly chest fly using resistance bands anchored behind you for constant tension through the arc.
exercises.setup: Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height, hold a handle in each hand, and step forward with a soft bend in your elbows.
exercises.instructions: Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, squeeze, then return with control to the stretched position.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout
Squeeze your chest at the center of the movement
Do not turn the fly into a press by bending your elbows too much
Stand tall with your core braced
Use a lighter band if you cannot control the return

exercises.name: Incline Cable Fly
exercises.description: A cable fly with pulleys set low and handles brought upward and together to emphasize the upper chest.
exercises.setup: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position, grab the handles, and step forward into a slight stagger stance with a soft bend in your elbows.
exercises.instructions: Bring the handles up and together in front of your upper chest in a sweeping arc, squeeze, then return with control.
formCues: Lead with your elbows and keep a fixed soft bend in your arms
Squeeze your upper chest at the top of the arc
Do not let your shoulders shrug toward your ears
Control the eccentric; do not let the weight pull you back abruptly
Use a slight forward lean for balance

exercises.name: Svend Press
exercises.description: A chest squeeze exercise performed by pressing two weight plates together in front of the body and extending the arms.
exercises.setup: Stand tall or sit on a bench holding two small weight plates together between your palms at chest height with your elbows out.
exercises.instructions: Squeeze the plates together hard as you press them forward until your arms are extended, then return with control to your chest.
formCues: Keep constant pressure squeezing the plates together
Press straight forward; do not let your shoulders roll forward
Use lighter plates and focus on the chest squeeze, not heavy weight
Keep your core braced if standing
Stop if you feel wrist or shoulder discomfort

exercises.name: Kettlebell Floor Press
exercises.description: A floor press performed with kettlebells, stopping when your upper arms touch the ground to limit shoulder stress.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell in each hand in the rack or bottom position at chest level.
exercises.instructions: Press the kettlebells up until your arms are extended, lower until your upper arms rest on the floor, pause briefly, and repeat.
formCues: Keep your wrist straight and the kettlebell stable in your grip
Stop when your upper arms touch the floor; do not bounce
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back during the press
Control the bells; do not let them drift outward at the top
Use a manageable weight; kettlebells are harder to balance than dumbbells

exercises.name: Kettlebell Bench Press
exercises.description: A chest press performed with kettlebells on a flat bench, pressing from chest level with a neutral or angled grip.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on a bench with a kettlebell in each hand at chest level, feet planted, and your wrists stacked over your elbows.
exercises.instructions: Press the kettlebells up until your arms are extended, lower them under control to chest level, and repeat.
formCues: Keep the kettlebells stable; do not let them roll in your hands
Control the weight on the way down
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your glutes on the bench
Press in a smooth path without flaring your elbows excessively
Use lighter weight than your dumbbell bench press until you are comfortable

exercises.name: Kettlebell Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up performed with each hand on a kettlebell handle to increase range of motion and add stability demands.
exercises.setup: Place two kettlebells on the floor shoulder-width apart, grip the handles, and set up in a high plank with your body in a straight line.
exercises.instructions: Lower your chest between the kettlebells by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension.
formCues: Keep the kettlebells from tipping; grip firmly and press evenly
Lower with control into the deeper range of motion
Keep your core braced and your hips in line with your shoulders
Do not let your shoulders dump forward at the bottom
Use standard push-ups first if balance on the bells is too difficult

exercises.name: Pilates Chest Expansion
exercises.description: A Pilates chest opener performed on a mat or reformer by reaching the arms back with control to stretch and open the chest and shoulders.
exercises.setup: On a mat, stand or kneel tall with your arms at your sides. On a reformer, kneel on the carriage facing the footbar and hold the straps behind you at hip height with light spring tension.
exercises.instructions: Inhale as you reach your arms back to open your chest, exhale as you return your arms forward or to your sides with control.
formCues: Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis; do not arch your lower back
Open through your chest without shrugging your shoulders up
Move your arms from your shoulder blades, not just your hands
On the reformer, control the springs on the return
Use small range first if your shoulders feel tight

exercises.name: Reformer Chest Press
exercises.description: A chest press on the reformer using spring resistance and handles or straps while lying or kneeling on the carriage.
exercises.setup: Lie or kneel on the reformer carriage facing away from the footbar, hold the handles at chest height, and set an appropriate spring tension.
exercises.instructions: Exhale as you press the handles forward until your arms are extended, inhale as you return with control to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your core engaged so your torso stays stable on the carriage
Press through your chest; do not lock out aggressively
Control the springs on the return; do not let them snap you back
Keep your shoulders away from your ears
Adjust spring tension to match your strength level

exercises.name: Reformer Long Box Push Through
exercises.description: A reformer exercise on the long box where you press through the footbar or straps in a forward arc to open and strengthen the chest.
exercises.setup: Lie prone on the long box on the reformer, reach forward to the footbar or straps, and set light to moderate spring tension.
exercises.instructions: Exhale as you press through the bar or straps, lengthening your arms and opening your chest, then inhale as you return with control.
formCues: Keep your hips anchored on the box throughout
Lead with your sternum and reach long through your arms
Do not collapse in your lower back as you press through
Use your breath to pace each rep
Start with lighter springs until you own the shoulder range

exercises.name: Reformer Chest Expansion
exercises.description: A kneeling reformer exercise that opens the chest by reaching the arms back against spring resistance.
exercises.setup: Kneel on the reformer carriage facing the footbar, hold the straps behind you at hip height, and set light spring tension.
exercises.instructions: Inhale as you reach your arms back to open your chest against the springs, exhale as you return your arms forward with control.
formCues: Keep your torso upright; do not lean forward as your arms move
Open your chest without flaring your ribs forward
Keep your shoulders down and your neck long
Control the springs on the return
Use lighter tension if you feel shoulder strain

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: A compound rowing exercise performed by hinging at the hips and pulling a barbell toward your lower chest or upper abdomen.
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, hinge forward with a flat back, and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width with your knees softly bent.
exercises.instructions: Pull the bar toward your lower chest, squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower the bar with control back to arm extension.
formCues: Keep your back flat; do not round your spine
Pull with your elbows driving back, not your hands yanking up
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the rep
Brace your core so your torso stays stable
Avoid using momentum from your hips to heave the weight

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight vertical pull performed by hanging from a bar and pulling your chin above the bar.
exercises.setup: Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with your palms facing away, hang with your arms extended, and brace your core.
exercises.instructions: Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, then lower with control back to a full hang.
formCues: Start from a dead hang with your shoulders engaged, not fully relaxed
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs
Avoid excessive swinging or kipping unless intentionally training that style
Lower under control through the full range of motion
Use an assisted band or machine if full pull-ups are too difficult

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A machine-based vertical pull that brings a wide bar down toward your upper chest to train the lats.
exercises.setup: Sit at the lat pulldown station, secure your thighs under the pad, grip the bar wider than shoulder-width, and sit tall with your chest up.
exercises.instructions: Pull the bar down to your upper chest, squeeze your lats, then return the bar with control to arm extension.
formCues: Pull the bar toward your chest, not behind your neck
Lean back slightly without rocking excessively
Drive your elbows down and back
Control the weight on the way up; do not let it pull you out of the seat
Keep your chest lifted throughout the rep

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: A seated horizontal row using a cable machine to pull a handle toward your torso while keeping your chest up.
exercises.setup: Sit at the cable row station with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, and grab the handle with your arms extended.
exercises.instructions: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return with control to arm extension.
formCues: Sit tall and keep your chest up throughout
Pull with your elbows close to your body
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the end of each rep
Do not round your lower back at the start of the pull
Control the return; do not let the weight jerk your shoulders forward

exercises.name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Row
exercises.description: A one-arm row performed with a dumbbell while supported on a bench to train each side of the back independently.
exercises.setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand with your arm extended, and keep your back flat.
exercises.instructions: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, squeeze your lat and shoulder blade, then lower with control to arm extension.
formCues: Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, not straight up to the ceiling
Keep your elbow close to your body
Avoid twisting your torso as you row
Complete all reps on one side before switching

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: A compound hip-hinge lift that pulls a barbell from the floor to a standing position, training the entire posterior chain.
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot, hinge down to grip the bar just outside your legs, and flatten your back with your chest up.
exercises.instructions: Drive through the floor, extend your hips and knees together, and stand tall with the bar, then reverse the motion to lower the bar under control.
formCues: Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift
Maintain a flat back; do not round your spine
Push the floor away rather than yanking with your lower back
Lock out by squeezing your glutes, not by leaning back excessively
Use proper bumper plates or raise the bar if flexibility limits your start position

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.description: A rowing exercise using a landmine barbell setup to pull weight toward your chest with a neutral grip handle.
exercises.setup: Straddle the bar with your feet on either side, hinge forward with a flat back, and grip the handle with both hands.
exercises.instructions: Pull the handle toward your lower chest, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower with control to arm extension.
formCues: Keep your back flat and your core braced
Pull with your elbows driving back
Avoid standing up taller as you pull the weight
Control the eccentric; do not let the weight slam at the bottom
Keep the bar path close to your torso

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A dumbbell row performed lying chest-down on an incline bench to isolate the back and reduce lower-back strain.
exercises.setup: Set an incline bench to about 30 to 45 degrees, lie chest-down with your feet planted, and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended.
exercises.instructions: Pull both dumbbells toward your hips, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower with control to arm extension.
formCues: Keep your chest glued to the pad throughout
Pull with your elbows close to your body
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top of each rep
Do not shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Use a controlled tempo; avoid swinging the dumbbells

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: A cable exercise that pulls a rope attachment toward your face with external rotation to target the upper back and rear shoulders.
exercises.setup: Set a cable pulley to upper-chest or face height, attach a rope, and grip it with your thumbs facing you as you step back into tension.
exercises.instructions: Pull the rope toward your forehead while separating your hands and rotating your elbows up and back, then return with control.
formCues: Pull toward your face, not your chest
Externally rotate at the end so your elbows finish high
Keep your ribs down; do not arch your lower back
Use lighter weight and focus on control and rear shoulder engagement
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the end of each rep

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight vertical pull performed with an underhand grip, emphasizing the lats and biceps.
exercises.setup: Grip a pull-up bar shoulder-width apart with your palms facing you, hang with your arms extended, and brace your core.
exercises.instructions: Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, then lower with control back to a full hang.
formCues: Start from a controlled hang with your shoulders engaged
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs
Avoid excessive swinging or kipping
Lower through the full range of motion under control
Use an assisted band or machine if needed

exercises.name: Barbell Biceps Curl
exercises.description: An isolation curl performed with a barbell to train the biceps through elbow flexion.
exercises.setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, grip a barbell underhand shoulder-width apart, and let your arms hang with your elbows at your sides.
exercises.instructions: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower with control back to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your elbows pinned at your sides throughout
Do not swing your hips or lean back to lift the weight
Control the lowering phase; do not drop the bar quickly
Use a full range of motion without hyperextending at the bottom
Keep your wrists straight and strong

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.description: A curl performed with dumbbells in a neutral grip to emphasize the biceps and brachialis.
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms at your sides.
exercises.instructions: Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders keeping your palms facing each other, then lower with control.
formCues: Keep your elbows close to your torso
Do not use momentum from your shoulders or hips
Maintain a neutral grip throughout the rep
Lower the dumbbells under control
Alternate arms if you prefer unilateral focus

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: A cable isolation exercise that extends the elbows to target the triceps by pushing a bar or rope downward.
exercises.setup: Set a cable pulley to the top position, attach a straight bar or rope, grip it with your elbows bent at your sides, and stand tall.
exercises.instructions: Push the attachment down until your arms are fully extended, squeeze your triceps, then return with control to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your elbows pinned at your sides
Do not let your shoulders roll forward
Extend fully at the bottom without hyperextending your elbows aggressively
Control the return; do not let the weight pull your arms up abruptly
Stand with a slight forward lean and braced core

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: An isolation shoulder exercise that raises dumbbells out to the sides to target the lateral deltoids.
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight bend in your elbows and your chest up.
exercises.instructions: Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms reach shoulder height, pause briefly, then lower with control.
formCues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout
Do not shrug the weight up with your traps
Stop around shoulder height; do not go excessively high
Use lighter weight and strict form over heavy swinging

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A pressing exercise that drives dumbbells overhead from shoulder height to train the shoulders and triceps.
exercises.setup: Sit on a bench with back support or stand tall, hold dumbbells at shoulder height with your palms facing forward or neutral, and brace your core.
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are extended, then lower with control back to shoulder height.
formCues: Keep your core braced and avoid excessive lower-back arch
Press in a smooth path without flaring your elbows too wide
Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder level
Do not bang the weights together at the top
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows

exercises.name: Lying Barbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A lying triceps exercise, often called a skull crusher, that lowers a barbell toward the forehead and extends the elbows to straighten the arms.
exercises.setup: Lie flat on a bench holding a barbell with a narrow overhand grip, arms extended above your chest, and your feet planted on the floor.
exercises.instructions: Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending your elbows, keep your upper arms still, then extend your elbows to press the bar back up.
formCues: Keep your upper arms vertical and fixed throughout
Lower with control; do not drop the bar toward your face
Extend fully at the top without locking out aggressively
Keep your wrists straight and elbows from flaring too wide
Use a manageable weight to protect your elbows

exercises.name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
exercises.description: A strict single-arm curl performed seated with your elbow braced against your inner thigh to isolate the biceps.
exercises.setup: Sit on a bench with your legs spread, hold a dumbbell in one hand, and brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
exercises.instructions: Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower with control to full extension.
formCues: Keep your upper arm pinned against your thigh
Do not swing your torso to lift the weight
Use a full controlled range of motion
Squeeze hard at the top of each rep
Complete all reps on one arm before switching

exercises.name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A triceps exercise performed by lowering a dumbbell behind the head with both hands and extending the elbows overhead.
exercises.setup: Stand or sit tall holding one dumbbell with both hands overhead, arms extended, and your core braced.
exercises.instructions: Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows, then extend your arms to press the weight back overhead.
formCues: Keep your upper arms close to your head and mostly still
Do not arch your lower back excessively as you press
Lower under control behind your head
Extend fully at the top without hyperextending your elbows
Use a weight you can control through the full range

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: A standing barbell press that drives the bar overhead from shoulder height to build shoulder and triceps strength.
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, grip the barbell just outside shoulder-width at collarbone height, and brace your core and glutes.
exercises.instructions: Press the bar straight overhead until your arms are extended, then lower with control back to the starting position.
formCues: Keep your core and glutes tight to avoid excessive back arch
Press the bar in a straight path close to your face
Tuck your chin slightly as the bar passes your head
Do not lean back excessively to finish the rep
Lock out with your biceps near your ears at the top

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
exercises.description: An isolation shoulder exercise that raises dumbbells in front of the body to target the front deltoids.
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with a slight bend in your elbows.
exercises.instructions: Raise the dumbbells forward until your arms reach shoulder height, pause briefly, then lower with control.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout
Raise to shoulder height, not above your head
Do not swing your hips or use momentum
Lower the dumbbells under control
Use lighter weight and focus on front shoulder engagement

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.description: A compound lower-body exercise performed with a barbell across your upper back, bending at the knees and hips to squat down and stand back up.
exercises.setup: Set the bar in a squat rack at upper-chest height, step under the bar with it resting across your upper traps or rear delts, grip the bar, and unrack by standing up with your feet shoulder-width apart.
exercises.instructions: Break at the hips and knees to squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive through your feet to stand back up.
formCues: Keep your chest up and your core braced throughout
Track your knees over your toes; do not let them collapse inward
Keep your heels planted and your whole foot in contact with the floor
Control the descent; do not drop into the bottom position
Use safety bars or a spotter when lifting heavy

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.description: A compound squat variation with the barbell racked across the front of the shoulders, emphasizing the quads with a more upright torso.
exercises.setup: Set the bar in a squat rack at chest height, rack it across your front delts with elbows high, unrack, and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
exercises.instructions: Break at the hips and knees to squat down while keeping your torso upright, then drive through your feet to stand back up.
formCues: Keep your elbows high so the bar stays secure on your shoulders
Stay upright; do not let your chest collapse forward
Track your knees over your toes
Keep your heels planted throughout the rep
Use clean grip or cross-arm grip based on wrist mobility

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip-hinge exercise that lowers a barbell along the legs with a slight knee bend to target the hamstrings and glutes.
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, hold a barbell at hip height with an overhand grip, and brace your core.
exercises.instructions: Push your hips back and lower the bar along your thighs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
formCues: Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the movement
Maintain a flat back; do not round your spine
Bend mostly at the hips with only a slight knee bend
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, not when your back rounds
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back excessively

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: A machine-based leg exercise where you press a weighted platform away using your legs while seated or angled in the leg press.
exercises.setup: Sit in the leg press machine with your back flat against the pad, feet shoulder-width on the platform, and release the safety handles.
exercises.instructions: Lower the platform by bending your knees until they reach about 90 degrees, then press through your feet to extend your legs without locking out aggressively.
formCues: Keep your lower back in contact with the pad; do not let it round off at the bottom
Do not lock your knees out hard at the top
Place your feet so your knees track over your toes
Control the weight on the way down; do not bounce at the bottom
Use a full but pain-free range of motion

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: An isometric hold that trains the entire core by maintaining a straight body line from head to heels.
exercises.setup: Start on the floor on your forearms and toes with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body in one straight line.
exercises.instructions: Hold the position while keeping your core braced and hips level, then rest when your form breaks down.
formCues: Keep your hips in line with your shoulders; do not sag or pike
Brace your abs as if preparing for a light punch
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor slightly ahead of your hands
Squeeze your glutes to help maintain a flat lower back
Breathe steadily throughout the hold

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: A floor-based core drill that alternates opposite arm and leg extensions while keeping the lower back pressed to the ground.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling, knees bent at 90 degrees, and your lower back flat against the floor.
exercises.instructions: Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg toward the floor, return to the start, and alternate sides while keeping your core braced.
formCues: Keep your lower back glued to the floor throughout
Move slowly and with control on each rep
Do not let your ribs flare as your arm and leg extend
Exhale as you extend and inhale as you return
Only extend as far as you can without losing back contact

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: A classic abdominal exercise that curls the upper body off the floor to train the rectus abdominis through spinal flexion.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and your hands lightly behind your head or crossed on your chest.
exercises.instructions: Curl your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs, pause briefly at the top, then lower with control.
formCues: Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck
Keep your lower back in contact with the floor at the bottom
Exhale as you crunch up and inhale on the way down
Use a small range of motion focused on the upper abs
Do not use momentum from your arms or hips

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: A dynamic core exercise that alternates elbow-to-knee twists to target the abs and obliques.
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head, legs lifted, and knees bent at about 90 degrees.
exercises.instructions: Bring your right elbow toward your left knee while extending your right leg, then switch sides in a pedaling motion.
formCues: Rotate through your torso, not by pulling on your neck
Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor
Move with control rather than rushing through reps
Fully extend the non-working leg without letting it drop to the floor
Exhale as you twist and crunch

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: An isometric hold performed on one side to strengthen the obliques and lateral core stabilizers.
exercises.setup: Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor, elbow under your shoulder, and your legs stacked or staggered.
exercises.instructions: Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet, hold, then lower and switch sides.
formCues: Keep your hips stacked and avoid rotating forward or backward
Drive through your forearm and bottom foot to stay elevated
Do not let your hips sag toward the floor
Keep your top shoulder pulled back and neck neutral
Breathe steadily throughout the hold

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: A hanging core exercise that raises the legs toward the chest to train the lower abs and hip flexors.
exercises.setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms extended, and your shoulders engaged away from your ears.
exercises.instructions: Raise your legs by curling your pelvis and lifting your knees or straight legs toward your chest, then lower with control.
formCues: Avoid excessive swinging; use controlled momentum if needed
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis at the top to engage the lower abs
Do not shrug your shoulders up toward your ears
Lower your legs slowly without arching your lower back excessively
Bend your knees to make the movement easier if needed

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.description: A kneeling cable exercise that uses spinal flexion and added resistance to overload the abdominal muscles.
exercises.setup: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley, kneel facing the machine, and hold the rope beside your head with your hips stacked over your knees.
exercises.instructions: Crunch down by rounding your spine and bringing your elbows toward your thighs, then return with control to the starting position.
formCues: Move by flexing your spine, not by sitting your hips back
Keep your hips fixed throughout the rep
Exhale hard as you crunch down
Use a full controlled range without bouncing at the bottom
Choose a weight that allows strict form

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.description: An anti-rotation core exercise that resists cable pull force while pressing the handle straight out from the chest.
exercises.setup: Set a cable pulley at chest height, stand sideways to the machine, and hold the handle at your chest with both hands.
exercises.instructions: Press the handle straight out in front of your chest, hold briefly against the rotational pull, then return to your chest with control.
formCues: Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front
Do not let the cable rotate your torso
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes
Press in a straight line from your sternum
Complete all reps on one side before switching

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.description: A seated rotational core exercise that twists the torso side to side, optionally holding a dumbbell for added resistance.
exercises.setup: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, heels lightly on the ground, torso leaned back slightly, and hold a dumbbell at your chest.
exercises.instructions: Rotate your torso to one side, then the other, keeping your chest up and moving through a controlled range.
formCues: Rotate from your ribcage, not just your arms
Keep your chest lifted and core braced
Do not round your lower back excessively
Move with control rather than whipping side to side
Keep your feet planted or lift them for a harder variation

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.description: A dynamic plank variation that alternates driving the knees toward the chest for core engagement and conditioning.
exercises.setup: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line, and your core braced.
exercises.instructions: Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in an alternating running motion while keeping your hips low.
formCues: Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists
Do not let your hips bounce up and down excessively
Maintain a braced core throughout
Land softly on the balls of your feet as you switch
Start slow and build speed only with good form
